activity.notes: Al-Ma'mun (Abu al-Abbas Abd Allah ibn Harun al-Rashid), seventh Abbasid caliph, reigned 813–833. He proclaimed himself caliph amid the struggle with al-Amin before Baghdad fell in 813; this Activity follows the conventional full caliphal reign dating of 813–833 and is not a lifetime or only-in-Baghdad period. He entered Baghdad in 819. His support for scholars and translation and the establishment of the Mihna in 833 belong to the reign context; this record does not assert sole foundation of the House of Wisdom.

sources.title: Maʾmun — Encyclopaedia Iranica (Clifford Edmund Bosworth)
sources.citation_text: Bosworth identifies Ma'mun as seventh Abbasid caliph (r. 813–833), describes the war with al-Amin and his arrival in Baghdad in 819.

sources.title: Maʾmūn — Biographical Encyclopedia of Astronomers, Max Planck Institute for the History of Science
sources.citation_text: Len Berggren's specialist biography documents Ma'mun's birth in 786, death in 833 and 813 accession as seventh Abbasid caliph; it discusses his learned patronage.

sources.title: Islam: Empire of Faith — Mamun (PBS)
sources.citation_text: PBS describes the caliph's 813–833 reign, succession conflict, Khurasan political base and scholarly translation patronage.

review_context.canonical_person_disambiguation: Seventh Abbasid caliph (786–833), son of Harun al-Rashid; not Ma'munid rulers of Khwarazm (10th–11th centuries).
